A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same occupation-kernel research. All 23 pages of v1 and 30 pages of v2, including equations, tables, figures, and appendices, support comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original ODE benchmark results in Table 3 and quasilinear PDE reconstruction experiments in Section 5.1 and Appendix H.

after.justification: V2 reports original ODE benchmark results in Table 2, pendulum and buoy experiments in Section 5, and runtime measurements in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The core ODE integral ridge-regression method and trapezoidal construction remain unchanged despite the OCK-to-MOCK renaming. However, v2 removes the quasilinear PDE-learning procedure from v1 Section 5 and Appendix G, and introduces a physics-constrained adaptation using nonseparable divergence-free Matérn kernels.

E1.justification: V2 retains the eight original ODE benchmark datasets, adds Lorenz96 at 1024 dimensions, and introduces synthetic pendulum and real ocean-buoy trajectories. It removes the grid-based quasilinear PDE reconstruction task and its experiments.

E2.justification: V2 adds Latent ODE, labeled Lode, throughout the main benchmark comparison. The existing Null, ResNet, SINDy-Poly, and three eDMD comparators remain; expanding v1's abbreviated table labels does not introduce additional methods.

E3.justification: V1's grid-search tuning becomes Bayesian optimization for MOCK in v2. New protocols include 100 pendulum trajectories with 50 samples each and retaining every tenth buoy observation. Appendix B.1 also changes the printed Lorenz96 term from -x_(k-1)^2 to -x_(k-1)x_(k-2), without establishing whether data were regenerated. Error formulas remain unchanged. V2's blanket 60/20/20 split statement conflicts with its retained 70/10/20 clinical-data descriptions, leaving actual clinical splits unresolved.

E4.justification: V2 adds comparisons across Gaussian, Laplace, Matérn, and random-feature kernels; scalar-versus-divergence-free kernel analyses on pendulum and buoy data; and comparative runtime scaling analyses. V1's PDE sample-size sensitivity and reconstruction-error analysis in Appendix H and Figure 3 are removed.

E5.justification: V1 reports one-sided Wilcoxon comparisons with three significance thresholds. V2 explicitly pairs trajectory errors, combines four kernel-specific Wilcoxon p-values using Fisher's method, and marks significance in either direction at p < 0.01. No repeated-run counts or confidence-interval reporting are introduced.

E6.justification: Main-table values and rankings are extensively revised. For Lorenz96-32, v1 reports SINDy Err 5 versus OCK 82; v2 reports SINDy 8.56 versus Gaussian MOCK 0.47. Changed tuning prevents interpreting this as a same-setting improvement. V2 also replaces clinical ResNet NA entries with numerical results, adds kernel, Latent ODE, 1024-dimensional, constraint, and runtime results, and removes the PDE outcomes.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 and its representer proof remain, but v1's weak-formulation Theorem 2, its proof, and the PDE derivations are removed. V2 adds constrained-kernel constructions, Hamiltonian relations, and comparator complexity derivations, and corrects the regularization factor in the explicit-kernel normal equation. Its new Appendix C.2 contains an inconsistency: d2 includes 15(r/sigma)^2 where the Section 5.1 derivative construction requires 15(r/sigma).

C1.justification: The central claim of learning ODE vector fields with linear dimensional scaling is retained. The claimed extension shifts from demonstrated PDE learning and weak-formulation justification to physics-constrained vector-field recovery. V2's abstract also introduces explicit claims of winning three of nine full-trajectory and four of nine next-point comparisons; PDE applications become future work.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations connecting two-point training to next-point performance, discusses Latent ODE initial-condition mismatch and kernel dependence, and interprets benefits from physical constraints. It explicitly defers convergence and noise-error analysis and qualifies runtime comparisons because hardware and tuning procedures differ. The underlying CMU heterogeneity caveat already existed in v1.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands implementation documentation: explicit quadrature formulas and algorithm inputs, data-file structure, the NumPy solver and version, Bayesian-optimization software and version, 200 random features, kernel formulas, and new dataset preprocessing. Figure 7 separates runtimes including and excluding hyperparameter tuning. Appendix A changes the code-capsule download target; clinical data remain restricted.

R1.justification: V2 develops a more explicit distinction from Rosenfeld and Russo's finite-feature formulation, emphasizing separable factorization and general matrix-valued kernels. It adds neural/latent ODE references and extensive divergence-free, curl-free, and constrained Gaussian-process literature, while removing much of the PINN, recurrent-network, and PDE-oriented positioning. This exceeds bibliographic or publication-status updates.

P1.justification: The title and method name change, and the introduction, background, contribution statements, and experimental narrative are substantially rewritten and reorganized. Comparator descriptions move into the experimental section and Appendix G, evaluation receives several dedicated subsections, and references move before the appendices.

P2.justification: The main results table changes from eight compact panels to nine larger panels with additional method rows. V2 adds an algorithm illustration, NFHN comparison plots, pendulum error maps, a buoy vector-field plot, and complexity/runtime displays. The PDE figure is removed. The original trajectory and biomarker figures are retained as Figures 2 and 4.

improvement.justification: V2 better exposes kernel dependence and competitor advantages through kernel comparisons and the Latent ODE baseline, while clearer algorithms and software details make the retained ODE method easier to implement. These benefits are tempered by removal of the weak-formulation/PDE development and unresolved reproducibility problems, particularly the conflicting clinical splits and the inconsistent expanded divergence-free kernel formula.
